title: How effective is matrix reordering for improving performance of sparse matrix-vector multiplication?
problem: Evaluating the effectiveness and consistency of matrix reordering strategies for optimizing sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) performance across different multicore CPU platforms.
motivation: SpMV is a critical kernel in many applications; matrix reordering can improve cache locality and load balance, but effectiveness varies across architectures. Systematic evaluation is needed to understand which reordering strategies work best on which platforms.
method: Experimental study comparing multiple matrix reordering strategies on different multicore CPUs (sequential and parallel execution); evaluates non-zero element pattern optimization for reducing data movement and improving load balance.
key_novelty: Systematic cross-platform evaluation of reordering strategies; addresses measurement methodology and consistency issues; analysis of load imbalance impact.
contributions: Comprehensive evaluation of matrix reordering impact on SpMV across multiple CPU architectures
Analysis of measurement methodology for fair comparison
Evaluation of consistency of reordering benefits across different machines
Study of load imbalance effects on reordering effectiveness
baselines: Different reordering strategies (RCM, Nested Dissection, etc.)
limitations: Abstract only; specific reordering strategies not named; no performance numbers provided; unclear if GPU architectures considered.
